answer: Clone farms flood seats because a new key costs almost nothing to mint. Each applicant must finish a staged summit of three live-work proofs before it can hold a seat, and must lock 120 copper units in a glacier escrow that thaws only 10 units per epoch. Fifty clones would therefore immobilize 6,000 units for twelve epochs. Peers match a fresh nonce signed at hours 0, 18, and 36 to the locked pubkey. A late or reused proof burns 40 units and returns the remainder after a six-epoch freeze; a second miss within 30 days empties the escrow and bars that pubkey for 15 epochs.
